title: Review: Graphs and data analysis; SI units and prefixes; Estimation and orders of magnitude; Scalars and vectors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS01-1#N.5, MS03-1#N.15, MS04-1#N.10, MS05-1#N.13, MS01-1#N.11a, MS04-1#N.3, MS05-1#N.4, MS01-1#N.7, MS04-1#N.6, MS01-1#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Gradient
items.clue: Δy divided by Δx, taken from a large triangle; it has its own units.

items.label: Reaction time
items.clue: Delay between a signal and a person's response: about 0.2 s for an adult.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Runs from the first tail to the last tip when arrows are drawn tip to tail.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Letter such as k, M or n placed before a symbol to stand for a power of ten.

questions.stem: A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: A best-fit line has gradient 2.50. The steepest line through all the error bars has gradient 2.65 (same units). What is the percentage uncertainty in the gradient?
A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?
Which equation cannot be correct, because it is not homogeneous? (s displacement, u and v velocities, a acceleration, t time)
questions.explanation: v² and u² are in m² s⁻², but 2at is in m s⁻¹. Terms with different units cannot be added, so this equation must be wrong.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?
What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².
